clue.text: Regrets accepting retreat with singular lack of civility

indicators.note: one word taking in another means it holds it inside

parts.note: to regret is to rue, so regrets is rues
a den is a private retreat or hideaway
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Someone sorry for withdrawing, but still rude, as a lone act of incivility.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudeness is simply impoliteness, the absence of good manners and courtesy.

clue.text: Implicated in failure in income control

indicators.note: implicated in suggests letters caught up inside a string of words

explanation.surface: Someone involved in failing to control income.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb or restrain something, as one pulls a horse's reins.

clue.text: Disappointing show discourages objections when second half is abandoned

parts.note: to dampen enthusiasm is to damp it, so discourages is damps

indicators.note: abandoning the second half drops the last four of the word's eight letters

parts.note: quibbles are petty objections

explanation.surface: A poor performance puts down complaints once the second half is cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp squib is a firework that fizzles, so an anticlimactic flop.

clue.text: Refusal to nurse at the outset is unacceptable

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: at the outset says to take only the opening letter of nurse

explanation.surface: Refusing to care for a patient from the start is improper.
explanation.definitionFit: Not on is a British idiom for something not permissible or out of order.

clue.text: Dishevelled politician left cider for a couple of fellows

indicators.note: the politician left, giving way to the fellows put in its place

parts.note: scrumpy is rough farmhouse cider from western England
an MP is a Member of Parliament
F is short for fellow, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: A politician abandons a drink to a pair of men.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRUMPY is strong, rough cider made in the West Country of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Scruffy means untidy and shabby in appearance.

clue.text: One small country such as Great Britain

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
land can mean a country or nation

explanation.surface: A modest nation compared with Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Britain is an example of a landmass surrounded by sea.

clue.text: Without reason extremely dear parents sadly broke up

indicators.note: sadly signals the remaining letters are put in disorder
without says the letters named next are removed
extremely picks the outermost letters of reason

explanation.surface: Beloved parents split up for no good reason, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes R and N (the ends of reason, by 'extremely') from DEARPARENTS; 'sadly' rearranges the remaining DEAPARETS.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple who broke up parted ways, splitting into two.

clue.text: A right to property overseas

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold another's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A legal claim on property abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien and overseas both mean foreign, from another country.

clue.text: Detectives essentially go off in different directions

parts.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors
per se is Latin for in itself, essentially

explanation.surface: Detectives basically split up to search.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter or spread out widely is to move apart.

clue.text: Young mum irate after being sacked

indicators.note: a place that has been sacked is left in disorder, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A mother is furious after losing her job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after being sacked' reads as losing a job, but it signals the rearrangement of MUM IRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something young is not yet fully grown or developed, the same as childish or unripe.

clue.text: Falls backwards going round old ruins

indicators.note: one piece going round another surrounds it
backwards says the word for falls is read from right to left

parts.note: to slip is to fall, so falls is slips

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles backwards among ancient ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' turns SLIPS into SPILS, which goes round O.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something is to wreck or mar it, which is what spoiling does.

clue.text: Agreement is loaded we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is said aloud like another

parts.note: something loaded is packed

explanation.surface: A treaty laden with conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a treaty or deal between parties.

clue.text: "Ghosts" he wrote "I believed simply errant nonsense at first"

indicators.note: at first says to take only the opening letter of each of the quoted words

explanation.surface: A critic's confession that the play Ghosts struck them as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen, the Norwegian dramatist, wrote the 1881 play Ghosts.

clue.text: Cologne newspaper carried the story of disembowelled corpse on Friday

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it, so the Friday letter comes first

parts.note: a rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper
a paper that ran a story carried it

indicators.note: with its insides removed, only the outer letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A German newspaper in Cologne reports a gruesome Friday murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cologne' looks like the German city, but it is eau de cologne, the scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne is a light perfume, so it is a scent or pleasant smell.

clue.text: Bob's dog gets testy regularly

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: regularly says to take every other letter of the word testy

explanation.surface: A man named Bob owns a dog that becomes irritable now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name, but it is the verb for a quick bow.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to make a quick bending movement of respect, a small curtsy.

clue.text: Temporary interns at work

indicators.note: set to work, the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Interns are short-term staff on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' looks like a phrase, but 'at' is part of the fodder and 'work' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Transient means passing or short-lived, not lasting.

clue.text: Offensive acting by student group leads to complaint

parts.note: the Tet Offensive was a 1968 campaign in the Vietnam War
A is an abbreviation for acting, as in a job title
the NUS is the UK's National Union of Students

explanation.surface: Rude theatrics by a student union provoke complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun: the Tet Offensive. 'complaint' here means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be a medical ailment, and lockjaw is one such disease.

clue.text: Unavoidable tax from the past collected in forthcoming year

indicators.note: something collected in is gathered inside

parts.note: the forthcoming future is near
a cess was an old local tax

explanation.surface: An old tax will inevitably be gathered next year.
explanation.definitionFit: Something necessary is essential and cannot be done without.

clue.text: Overcome on French climb

parts.note: sur is French for on
to mount is to climb

explanation.surface: Conquering a French ascent.
explanation.definitionFit: To surmount an obstacle is to get over it, beat it.

clue.text: Shaking bum with fury causes offence

indicators.note: shaking things mixes them up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: rage is a synonym of fury

explanation.surface: Wiggling one's backside angrily is a rude display.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to take offence; the noun means resentment or affront.

clue.text: Gain attention by yawning halfway through

parts.note: to give an ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: halfway through picks the central letter of yawning

explanation.surface: Getting someone's attention while yawning midway.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to gain or acquire something by work.

clue.text: Headless naked figures around the church offer temptation

indicators.note: turned around, the trimmed word is read backwards
headless says the first letter of the word is lost

parts.note: nudes are naked figures in art
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Nude statues near a church tempt passers-by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headless' drops the first letter of the naked figures, and 'around' then turns the remaining UDES back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure someone into wrongdoing or desire is to tempt them.

clue.text: Sign of measles first appears after spot spread across my back

indicators.note: a piece that appears after another goes at the end
one piece spread across another wraps it
spread out, the letters of spot are rearranged
back says my is read from the end
first takes only the opening letter of measles

explanation.surface: A measles rash spreads across someone's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges the spot letters as SPTO; 'across' wraps them round 'my back', read backwards; the measles letter, picked by 'first', comes last by 'appears after'.
explanation.definitionFit: A symptom is an indication of disease, a telltale mark.

clue.text: He is liable to get dressed up without a shirt

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means wrapped around
up in a down clue says the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: robed means dressed
a T is a T-shirt

explanation.surface: A man must dress up without a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but means outside: DEBOR (ROBED read 'up') goes around T.
explanation.definitionFit: A debtor owes money, so he is the one liable to pay.

clue.text: Mom alerts doctor to confused state

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered

explanation.surface: A mother calls the doctor about someone's confused state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' reads as a noun, but it is the verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a whirlpool, figuratively a state of turmoil and chaos.

clue.text: Directions reached me by word of mouth from the opposing camp

parts.note: E, N, E are compass directions, east-north-east

indicators.note: by word of mouth says the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: in casual speech my is said like me

explanation.surface: Instructions reached someone orally from the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: Enemy, as an adjective, describes hostile forces on the opposing side.

clue.text: Hurry to get back in upsets a horserider

indicators.note: to get back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Rushing to return to a scene where a rider was thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is speed or urgency, the noun sense of hurry.

clue.text: Slaughter half cut gangster

indicators.note: cut says the word is shortened, losing its last letter

parts.note: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A drunken mobster kills someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' looks like British slang for drunk, but 'cut' trims HALF to HAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal is meat killed according to Islamic law, so it describes a mode of butchery.

clue.text: Sawn off weapon's still irregular

indicators.note: like a sawn-off shotgun, the word loses its front letter

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
still water is even, calm and flat

explanation.surface: A sawn-off shotgun is still unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irregular is not smooth or level, lacking uniformity.

clue.text: Strong growth following last reorganisation

indicators.note: one piece following another comes after it
a reorganisation rearranges things, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: a wart is a small growth on the skin

explanation.surface: Robust growth after a final shake-up of a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwart means sturdy and robust, loyally dependable.

clue.text: Go by the streets either way for secret rendezvous

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: either way says these letters read the same in both directions

parts.note: ST is short for street, so streets gives STS

explanation.surface: Walking the streets on the way to clandestine meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: Trysts are lovers' private appointments, secret meetings.

clue.text: Master scheme is adopted in less than half of emergencies

indicators.note: something adopted in a family is taken inside it
less than half of says to take only the opening few letters of the word

parts.note: a ploy is a cunning scheme

explanation.surface: A clever plan is adopted in an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than half of' takes EMER, four of the eleven letters of emergencies.
explanation.definitionFit: A master is a boss who hires workers, the opposite of a servant.
